idea-plugin.name: open-java-format
idea-plugin.description:
Formats Java code with open-java-format, a maintained fork of palantir-java-format: 120 columns, 4-space indents and lambda-friendly line breaking.

With the plugin enabled, Reformat Code runs open-java-format instead of the IDE's built-in Java formatter, and Optimize Imports removes unused imports and sorts the others as open-java-format does, so the IDE and your build produce identical files. The IDE's own Java code style settings no longer apply.

To format and fix imports on every save, tick Reformat code and Optimize imports under Tools → Actions on Save; Optimize imports before a commit and in the Reformat Code dialog runs open-java-format too. Imports the IDE adds as you type follow the same layout, unless the project's .editorconfig sets Java code style properties.

The formatter runs inside the IDE, with no process to start for a file, whatever version the project SDK is. A project that applies the dev.openjavaformat.java-format Gradle plugin takes the formatter version from the build; every other project uses the version bundled with this plugin.

The plugin's settings page offers two other ways to run it. In a separate JVM runs it on the IDE's runtime, the project SDK or another JDK of the IDE, Java 21 or later, and parses the syntax of that JDK's version. Native binary runs the formatter compiled for your platform, which the plugin downloads, in a Maven, Gradle or any other project; a binary of your own works too.

Requires IntelliJ IDEA 2024.2 or later, or another IDE with Java support such as Android Studio.
